Customer to share 500-row sample prompt set and expected labels by 2026-08-24
Schedule 2-hour pilot bench run week of 2026-08-31

summary: Discovery/POC scoping for Aerometrics: narrow open-model shortlist for multilingual (EN/ES/PT) maintenance-document extraction + conversational troubleshooting, define success criteria (accuracy targets, latency SLOs), estimate workload sizing and pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: share shortlist + bench template, customer to provide sample prompts and labels, schedule pilot run end of month.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (F1, exact match, latency p95)
Multilingual coverage and domain adaptation (avionics manuals)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the account lead for this engagement. quick intros?
[00:09] Priya Nair: hi, i'm Priya, head of ML at Aerometrics, we're responsible for the diagnostics and maintenance assistant project.
[00:15] Carlos Mendez: Carlos here, CTO — i'll be involved for infra/security questions.
[00:19] Samir Patel: Samir, SRE — i'll run the pilot infra with you.
[00:23] Liam O'Connor: Liam, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll own the bench and model tradeoffs.
[00:28] Lea Becker: Lea, localization — We'll need Spanish and Portuguese support, prioritizing safety-critical phrases.
[00:35] Maya: great. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist, bench plan, timelines, and open questions.
[00:44] Priya: the top-level goal is twofold: 1) extraction from maintenance manuals — high precision on action items and component IDs; 2) a conversational assistant for techs to ask "what torque spec for bolt X" — so both extraction and retrieval/QA.
[00:58] Liam: are you expecting a single model to do both or mix (extractor + smaller reranker)?
[01:04] Priya: ideally one for simplicity, but we can split if perf or accuracy suggests it. main thing is thresholds: extraction F1 > 0.88 and for QA exact-match on spec fields > 0.82. Latency target sub-200ms for short-turn queries, p95 under 350ms.
[01:28] Maya: good, that's actionable. on workload — what qps and dataset size are you expecting during pilot and at scale?
[01:34] Samir: pilot ~50 qps peak for 2 hrs/day, production target ~120 qps sustained with bursts to 220. Document corpus ~150k pages, but per-day inference is relatively low — roughly 10k doc lookups/day.
[01:50] Liam: so we'll design bench for both steady-state and burst. We'll test tokenized lengths — manuals are long; retrieval + prompt length could be 1k-2k tokens.
[02:03] Carlos: security corner: we need data residency + KMS integration if we go private. also likely SOC2 and iso27001 proof for enterprise.
[02:13] Maya: understood — we have hosted and private options. for POC, customers often start with hosted sandbox with redwood-managed keys or a VPC-hosted private trial. do you have a preference?
[02:24] Carlos: prefer VPC trial if possible, to mirror network constraints, but hosted sandbox is fine for initial bench if network egress is an issue.
[02:33] Priya: one question on models: we want open models because of licensing and quantization options — can you recommend shortlist?
[02:41] Liam: sure. initial shortlist we'd like to test: Llama-2-Chat-13B (quantized 4/8-bit), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct (or a trimmed variant), and GPT-NeoX-20B or mosaicide variant. we also include a distilled or 8-bit tuned variant to test latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:02] Lea: will these handle Spanish and Portuguese well?
[03:06] Liam: Llama-2 family and Mistral have decent multilingual coverage, but we'll need to bench them on domain prompts. For high coverage, we might test a translation+monolingual flow vs native multilingual model.
[03:18] Priya: domain adaptation — is few-shot enough or will we need fine-tuning?
[03:22] Liam: for extraction tasks, prompt engineering + retrieval-augmented prompts often get you 0.05–0.12 lift in F1. For the component-id exact-match, a small instruction-tuned or LoRA fine-tune on 2–5k labeled examples can move you further. we'll include both approaches in the bench matrix.
[03:42] Maya: quick check — success criteria recap: extraction F1 >= 0.88, exact match >= 0.82, p95 latency < 350ms for short queries, cost per 1k tokens under target (we'll ask pricing later). everyone comfortable?
[03:58] Priya: yes.
[04:00] Samir: cost target — we need to quantify; we'll accept a higher cost in pilot but production needs to be reasonable.
[04:08] Liam: ok, bench plan: we'll run the same prompt set across 4 model candidates, measure token usage, latency (client->model->response), p50/p95/p99, and accuracy metrics (F1, EM), plus memory/throughput with batch sizes. we'll also run quantized variants and repeat tests for English and Spanish prompts.
[04:31] Maya: we'll share a bench spreadsheet with columns for model, variant, quantization, token counts, p95 latency, F1, EM, and infra notes.
[04:40] Priya: timeline?
[04:42] Maya: proposed timeline: share shortlist + bench template within 2 business days, customer returns sample prompts/labels within 5 business days, bench run week of 2026-08-31 (2–3 days), review call week of 2026-09-07, then pilot refinement through September. does that align?
[04:59] Carlos: yes, that works.
[05:02] Lea: on localization, we'll provide a 200-row Spanish/pt sample to validate hallucination on spec numbers.
[05:10] Liam: great. another tradeoff: bigger models (40B) often score better on complex cross-sentence extraction but cost and latency are substantially higher; 7B/13B with retrieval + tuned prompts can match on many structured-extraction tasks. we'll capture that in the bench.
[05:29] Priya: what about on-device or edge? we might want a trimmed model for tablets in maintenance bays.
[05:36] Samir: yes, offline mode is desirable — sync when network available.
[05:40] Liam: for on-device, we look at 7B quantized 4-bit variants; we'll include a mobile latency row but full on-device build is out of POC scope unless you want an extended pilot.
[05:52] Maya: security again — Carlos, can you outline must-have controls for pilot?
[05:56] Carlos: SSO/SAML, audit logs for API calls, KMS for key separation, and ability to configure egress rules. also we need to review redwood's SOC2 attestation and network diagram.
[06:09] Maya: we'll send the one-pager + SOC2 evidence.
[06:12] Priya: any benchmark infra recommendations? we prefer a reproducible infra as code layout.
[06:16] Liam: we'll provide terraform snippets for both hosted and VPC-based bench; benchmark script runs are containerized, and we can share run logs and perf traces.
[06:27] Priya: what about caching? many of our prompts repeat.
[06:31] Liam: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching — for repetitive prompt prefixes you can get big improvements; we'll test cache-hit scenarios versus cold runs. we'll include a cache-hit column in the bench.
[06:44] Lea: safety — we need to ensure maintenance guidance never suggests unsafe procedures. how do you evaluate safety tuning?
[06:52] Liam: we'll add safety evaluation examples and measure failure modes; also add guardrails and post-processing rules; if required we can test a constrained decoding setup.
[07:02] Maya: ok, any competitors or other vendors you are evaluating?
[07:06] Priya: we're talking to a couple: OpenAI for hosted, Anthropic for safety-oriented baseline, and a smaller inference vendor for on-prem options.
[07:15] Maya: good to know. we'll make sure our bench highlights latency and cost advantages for the chosen models.
[07:20] Samir: can Redwood run the bench on our VPC so we see realistic network topology?
[07:25] Liam: yes — we can run tests in your VPC; we'll need a short-lived service account and some firewall rules.
[07:33] Priya: about metrics — for extraction, do you propose token-level F1 or entity-level?
[07:38] Liam: entity-level F1 for component IDs and action items; token-level for nuance metrics. exact-match for numeric specs. we'll include both.
[07:47] Maya: questions from our side: what are your acceptance criteria for moving from POC to pilot?
[07:52] Priya: if extraction F1 >= 0.88 and p95 latency < 350ms on VPC tests, and cost projection within 3x acceptable threshold, we move to a 90-day pilot with more integration.
[08:07] Maya: noted.
[08:09] Liam: one more technical note: model KV cache sizing — for long manuals we often rely on retrieval so KV cache growth is lower. we'll monitor memory on the bench.
[08:20] Carlos: also please include failover strategy — if a model exceeds latency, automatic fallback to smaller variant with lower-quality but guaranteed latency.
[08:30] Liam: Redwood's routing supports model fallbacks by policy; we'll include a recommended policy.
[08:36] Priya: what about telemetry and observability?
[08:39] Nadia Alvarez: (CSM) we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards; we'll demo that in the review.
[08:49] Priya: cool.
[08:51] Maya: to wrap, i'll send the shortlist + bench template and SOC2 one-pager by 2026-08-21. Priya team to send labeled sample and localization rows by 2026-08-24. we'll schedule bench run week of 2026-08-31 and review week of 2026-09-07.
[09:06] Carlos: sounds good.
[09:08] Priya: one small ask — include a baseline with simple retrieval + smaller model to compare with large-model answers.
[09:16] Liam: yes, baseline will be included.
[09:20] Lea: can you also mark examples where hallucination risk is high? we'll annotate that in the sample.
[09:27] Maya: absolutely. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links.
[09:31] (Meeting ends)
